item.title: Val Chmerkovskiy Benched From “Dancing With The Stars” Over “Fresh Prince” Post
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Val Chmerkovskiy was benched from "DWTS" after a "Fresh Prince" post drew backlash over its link to Will Smith's Oscars slap.
item.content:encoded:
Val Chmerkovskiy sat out the October 20 episode of “Dancing With the Stars” over a “Fresh Prince” post. His reference to Will Smith’s Oscars slap sparked backlash after a clash over his wife’s dance.

BBC Studios, which makes the show, barred the pro dancer for one week on October 17. He had taken aim at judge Carrie Ann Inaba. She had found fault with a dance by his wife, Jenna Johnson, and her partner, Harry Shum Jr.

“You almost saw Fresh Prince enter the ballroom last night,” Val wrote in a TikTok post that he later deleted.

The line was seen as a nod to Smith’s 2022 Oscars slap of Chris Rock. Val said he meant the meme about keeping his wife’s name out of the discussion, not what else those words might imply.

His response did not spare him a week on the bench. Jenna Dewan, his partner on the show, danced with Alan Bersten instead. Bersten had already been knocked out of the contest with his own partner.

“The well-being of everyone who works on Dancing with the Stars is non-negotiable,” BBC Studios said in a statement. The company said Val’s post fell short of the standards it expects from people who work on the show.

It all began with Harry and Johnson’s samba to Usher’s “Yeah!” featuring Lil Jon and Ludacris during Super Bowl Night. Inaba wanted more samba steps and said there had been a lift. When Johnson asked about the call, the judge read out the rule.

Two other dancers had helped Harry leave the floor for a backflip. Johnson said that, in most lift calls, one of the main partners had lifted the other. Still, she accepted that Inaba had a job to do. The pair earned 33 out of 40.

Val said he was sorry and had reached out to her directly. After he was barred from the show, he said his bid to defend his wife had been a bad call.

“Carrie Ann certainly didn’t deserve to get caught in the middle of my bad judgment, and I hate that she was,” he said.

Smith’s clash with Rock followed a joke about Jada Pinkett Smith’s hair. The “Fresh Prince” remark also hit close to home for this cast. Alfonso Ribeiro hosts the show, while Tatyana Ali is in the race for the trophy.

Dewan and Bersten performed a Viennese waltz to The Righteous Brothers’ “Unchained Melody” in honor of her mother, Nancy.

item.title: The Cover Art Is Already a Music Video: How Independent Rappers Are Using AI Visuals
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: Independent artists are using AI image-to-video tools to transform cover art and press photos into music visualizers, promotional clips, and social content without expensive video shoots.
item.content:encoded:
Pink-and-blue vinyl spinning on a turntable. Photo: Lee Campbell via Wikimedia Commons, CC0.

The record is mixed. The cover is approved. The release date is locked. Then somebody asks the question that stalls a lot of independent rollouts: what are we posting for the next four weeks?

Labels have creative teams for that. Independent artists usually have themselves, a homie with a camera, and a phone full of studio snapshots. A proper video shoot can cost more than the whole EP, and one video doesn’t cover a modern rollout anyway. A single now needs a teaser, a visualizer, a stream of vertical clips, and a looping canvas for the streaming page.

That gap is where a lot of artists are bringing in AI image-to-video. Not to replace the big shoot for the lead single, but to keep the visuals moving between the moments that matter.

Start With What You Already Own

Here’s the key shift: you don’t have to invent a visual world from a blank prompt. You already have one. It’s on the cover.

Image-to-video tools take a still you own, like cover art, a press photo or a shot from the session, and add motion: smoke drifting, neon flickering on wet pavement, a slow push toward the artist. Because the model works from your actual artwork, the look stays on-brand instead of drifting into somebody else’s aesthetic.

There are plenty of options. CapCut is still the go-to editor for a lot of artists cutting vertical content. Freebeat and Neural Frames are built around audio-reactive, beat-synced visuals. And all-in-one workspaces like MixVio put several image-to-video models, including Seedance, Kling and Veo, in one place, alongside image, voiceover and music tools, and show the credit cost before every run.

Let the Hook Set the Pace

A visual for a rap record should move like the record. Before you generate anything, listen to the hook and decide what kind of motion matches it.

  • A slow, heavy beat suits drifting smoke, a slow push-in and long holds.
  • A fast, bouncy hook suits quicker cuts, camera shake and flashing light.
  • A moody, late-night record suits rain, reflections and low streetlight.

Write that into the prompt in plain camera language: “slow push-in, smoke rising, red neon reflecting on wet pavement, artist nods to the beat.” Keep it simple. The more you ask for, the more likely faces and hands start to warp.

Build the Visual Pack

Here’s a lean way to cover a single for weeks of posting:

1.  Pick 4 to 6 strong stills. Cover art, two press shots, a location photo, a studio candid. High resolution, clear subject.

2.  Animate each for a few seconds. Most image-to-video routes produce clips of about 3 to 15 seconds, which is plenty for a hook. On MixVio’s image-to-video generator, you can set 9:16, 16:9 or 1:1 before you generate, so you’re not cropping later.

3.  Run two or three takes per still. Keep the ones that sit right on the tempo.

4.  Cut on the snare. Drop the clips into your editor and cut on the drums or the bar changes. That’s what turns AI clips into a music video instead of a slideshow.

5.  Export for every slot. Vertical for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, horizontal for YouTube, and a short loop for the streaming canvas.

If you need the same artist to show up consistently across several clips, look at reference-based generation, sometimes called reference-to-video. Instead of one start frame, you upload a small pack of images, for example the artist, the car and the block, and the model tries to keep all of them recognizable in a new scene. It’s not perfect, but it helps with the “why does he look different in every clip” problem.

Keep the Artist at the Center

AI visuals can make a rollout look cheap if you lean on them too hard.

  • Don’t fake the artist. Fans follow a real person. Use AI for atmosphere and world-building, and keep real footage and real photos of the artist up front.
  • Performance shots still need a camera. Lip-sync over a full verse isn’t reliable yet. Film the bars; animate the world around them.
  • Avoid the default look. If every rapper uses the same trendy style, nobody stands out. Build a consistent visual identity for the project and stick with it.
  • Wide beats close-up. Environmental shots hold up better than tight shots of faces and hands.

Rights Don’t Disappear Because It’s AI

This is the part people skip. Only animate images you own or have permission to use. If a photographer shot your press photos, check that your agreement covers new edits. If someone else is in the frame, get their okay.

Check commercial terms too. Many tools, MixVio included, reserve commercial use for paid plans and treat free outputs as test material. AI visuals don’t change anything about samples either. Clear the music the same way you always would.

Quick Answers

How long should an AI visualizer be? Long enough to carry the hook. For Shorts and Reels, 10 to 20 seconds built from several short clips usually works better than one long generated shot.

Image-to-video or text-to-video? If you already have cover art or photos, start with image-to-video, because it keeps your look. Text-to-video is better for brainstorming scenes you haven’t shot or drawn yet.

Will fans care that it’s AI? Some will. Being upfront about which parts are generated, and keeping the artist real on screen, goes a long way.

The Bottom Line

AI won’t direct your next big video, and it shouldn’t. But for independent artists running a release with no video budget, it’s a practical way to turn assets you already have into a steady run of visuals that actually sound like the record. Start with the cover, animate one image, cut it to the hook, and see what your audience does with it. The best rollouts have always been about ideas over budget. That part hasn’t changed.

item.title: Golden Globes Awards Committee Rejects Michael Jackson Biopic’s Musical Classification
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Michael Jackson's screen portrayal is tested as Golden Globes officials questioned its musical genre eligibility.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Jackson’s highly anticipated biopic Michael has been rejected from the Golden Globes’ musical or comedy categories after an awards committee determined the film’s musical performances did not sufficiently advance its storyline, according to Gold Derby.

Michael Jackson‘s cinematic legacy now has a more complicated pathway to win awards on the big night.

The biographical movie about the King of Pop was submitted by Lionsgate for consideration as a musical or comedy, but the Golden Globes awards committee determined that the production did not satisfy its requirements for that classification.

According to an exclusive report from Gold Derby, committee members concluded that the musical sequences in Michael were insufficient to qualify the movie as a musical under the organization’s established guidelines.

The decision could create a considerably tougher path toward Golden Globe recognition for Jaafar Jackson, who portrays his legendary uncle in the film.

Rather than competing against performers in the musical or comedy categories, Jackson would face actors in the drama division, traditionally regarded as a formidable field.

The controversy centers on a fundamental question about the movie itself. Is Michael primarily a dramatic examination of an extraordinary entertainer or a musical experience built around his celebrated catalog?

The Golden Globes apparently believe the answer is drama.

Under the organization’s rules, “a musical can be a comedy or a drama in which songs are used in addition to spoken dialogue to further the plot.”

According to Gold Derby, committee members determined that the performances featured in Michael did not sufficiently advance the storyline to meet that standard.

It is a movie chronicling an artist whose recordings, choreography and elaborate stage productions transformed popular entertainment. Despite Michael Jackson’s enormous musical influence, the committee reportedly viewed the film’s songs and performances as insufficient to establish its eligibility in the musical category.

Lionsgate may still challenge the determination.

The studio is reportedly considering an appeal before the Oct. 31 submission deadline. Should Lionsgate pursue that option, the awards committee would review its arguments and decide whether to reconsider the classification.

It should be noted that Bohemian Rhapsody (2018) was classified as a drama, not a musical or comedy, by the Golden Globes. The massively successful film competed in the drama categories at the 2019 Golden Globes.

Without a successful appeal, Michael and its leading performers would also compete in the drama categories.

Actor Colman Domingo would not encounter the same genre-related complication in supporting actor consideration because the Golden Globes combine supporting performances across musical, comedy and drama productions.

Following the Golden Globe victories of Ray and Walk the Line in musical or comedy categories, eligibility requirements were revised to distinguish conventional musical storytelling from dramatic biographies featuring musical performances.

Subsequent productions including Bohemian Rhapsody, Elvis and A Complete Unknown entered the Golden Globes competition as dramas.

Fans suggesting there was “hate” behind the decision were definitely wrong in this instance.

The ruling against Michael is consistent with an established awards precedent rather than an isolated judgment about Jackson’s legacy.

For Jaafar Jackson, the film represents an opportunity to portray one of entertainment’s most recognizable figures while establishing his own credentials as an actor.

item.title: Gunna Joins 100-Hit Club With “Pop It” Chart Debut
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Gunna reached 100 career Hot 100 entries with "Pop It," adding a chart milestone after he launched his own record label.
item.content:encoded:
Gunna reached 100 career Hot 100 entries with “Pop It.” The chart feat came less than two weeks into his new role as a label boss.

The song entered at No. 55 on the chart dated October 24, Billboard reported. The count spans his own songs and guest turns. He was the 25th act to reach that mark in the chart’s 68-year run.

“Pop It” drew 4.6 million U.S. streams and 4.7 million radio audience impressions during the October 9-15 tracking week. Billboard based the U.S. totals on figures from Luminate. Gunna joined J. Cole, Ariana Grande and Rod Wave as the fourth act to cross the 100-entry line this year.

His path started in June 2018 with a guest spot on Lil Baby’s “Life Goes On.” Lil Uzi Vert also appeared on the song. Later that year, “Drip Too Hard” with Lil Baby climbed to No. 4. He has since scored top-10 hits with “Lemonade,” “Pushin P” and “Fukumean.”

“Pop It” also marked a shift in Gunna’s work beyond the charts. Gunna released the song on October 9. That same day, he launched SB THE LABEL.

With Atlantic Music Group behind the venture, Gunna took the CEO seat. His first roster had three acts from Atlanta: Casper Bluff, Nechie and Dracc. Nechie had worked with Gunna before they joined forces under the new imprint. The roster put Gunna in a role that reached beyond his own songs.

The rollout brought both sides of that plan together. The “Pop It” video had the label’s new signees and tennis star Coco Gauff. In the Spike Jordan-directed clip, Gauff joined Gunna on the court for a first look at his new label.

The song gave fans a taste of “Splurge,” which he has teased as his next studio album. His last album, “The Last Wun,” came out in August 2025 with 25 tracks.

At the launch, he called the first three acts his brothers and spoke of room to grow in his new role.

“SB the Label represents the beginning of a new chapter for me,” he said in the launch statement.

item.title: 50 Cent And Tia Kemp Exchange Vicious Insults After Rick Ross’ Son Pistol-Whipped Madness
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: 50 Cent revives his 2009 magazine photo shoot with Tia Kemp as a new feud erupts over the pistol-whipping of Rick Ross' son.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent made the alleged pistol-whipping involving Rick Ross‘ son into a promo opportunity. And this time the feud is with BM Tia Kemp, who is firing back with some exceptionally personal ammunition. Y’all know she is not for play.

And there is an unusual twist to this story. These two actually posed together for a magazine photo shoot years ago!

The latest episode began when reports surfaced that William Roberts III, the son of Rick Ross and Tia Kemp, was pistol-whipped and threatened near Bethune-Cookman University in Daytona Beach, Florida. I do not think this was minor. I think that man was really considering major violence.

A 20-year-old suspect was reportedly arrested in connection with the incident and charged with aggravated assault and aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

Now, you would think something this serious might temporarily suspend the longstanding hostilities between 50 Cent and Rick Ross. Apparently, you would be mistaken.

50 declared that he would bond out the suspect accused of attacking Ross’ son. All he needed was his name. That was enough to send Tia Kemp into an absolute fury.

Kemp took to Instagram with a blistering response that targeted 50 Cent’s son, Sire, and his mother, Daphne Joy. Here we go again.

“Btchhhh azzzz @50cent U wanna play? U have NO room to post anyone’s child when urs on the spectrum and the reason being this hoooo was still swallowing 10,000 gallons of C****M when she was pregnant wit Sire!! 100 emotional Simp ahhhh btchhhhh!! “

That is a remarkable amount of venom, even by the standards of hatred. Got damn.

For clarity, Kemp’s allegation about Sire is not even verified.

Of course, 50 Cent was not about to surrender the final word.

He responded by posting the photograph from a their 2009 Smooth magazine photo shoot. Yes, before this latest verbal warfare, the two had actually participated in a magazine shoot together during the earlier days of 50’s notorious rivalry with Rick Ross. I did not realize this went so far back. WOW. Rappers really know. how to waste time beefing.

These people have been entangled in each other’s business for a long, long time.

“Damn Tia you sound tougher than ya boy, I ain’t got time to argue with you,” 50 wrote. “You see my new movie STREET FIGHTER it’s #1”

Only 50 Cent could resurrect a 17-year-old magazine shoot, insult somebody and squeeze in a movie promotion simultaneously.

We need to maintain some focus.

William Roberts III was allegedly the victim of a violent encounter. Now, we are bringing sons and other family into it.

What a lame spectacle.They all old heads too.

Tia Kemp is not intimidated by 50 Cent, and 50 appears perfectly comfortable keeping the controversy alive.

I just hope the young people involved can escape the circus.

What do you think? Has this feud finally crossed a line?

item.title: Jill Scott’s South African Tour Finale Canceled Weeks Before Shows
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jill Scott's South African tour finale was canceled, with refunds promised for both November shows and no new dates announced.
item.content:encoded:
Jill Scott‘s fans in South Africa will get their money back instead of the two shows set to close her world tour.

Showtime Management called off both dates on October 19, with less than three weeks to go before the first show. The firm cited “unforeseen circumstances” but did not say what went wrong.

Scott had been due at SunBet Arena in Pretoria on November 7. The next stop was Grand Arena, GrandWest, in Cape Town on November 11. Ticketmaster has marked both shows as canceled and stopped sales.

Fans will not need to file a claim to get all of their money back. The money will go back to the account used to buy the tickets. The Citizen said that could take five to 10 business days.

Those whose old card or bank details no longer work should watch for an email from the ticket seller with the next steps. The firm will also send buyers updates on their refunds.

There is no new date on the books yet, though Scott’s team has not ruled out a return.

“Jill and her team are exploring the possibility of returning to South Africa at a future date,” Showtime said in a statement, as quoted by TimesLIVE.

The lost dates were meant to cap a tour that spanned much more than those two cities. Scott and Live Nation Urban first announced a tour through the U.S., Europe, the U.K. and South Africa in March. GrandWest billed Cape Town as the last stop.

The “To Whom This May Concern World Tour” took its name from Scott’s sixth album, her first in more than ten years. Her plan for the shows put a live band at the heart of each night, with sets shaped for each city and a mix of soul, jazz and spoken word.

She last played South Africa at the DStv Delicious Festival two years ago. This time, fans had been promised two shows of her own.

Scott moved four Texas shows to new dates in September after she tested positive for COVID-19 in August. The new statement gave no link to that illness. It also gave no date for her next South African show.

item.title: Chris Brown’s “Party” Producer Sues Sony For $1.25M Over Royalty Dispute
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Chris Brown's "Party" producer sued Sony for nearly $1.25 million, alleging a shortfall in pay and delays to a rights sale.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Brown‘s “Party” producer sued Sony Music for nearly $1.25 million over a pay dispute and a stalled rights deal. The suit claims the label paid him half the rate he was owed, then held up a change in who would get the checks.

Ishmael Sadiq Montague, known as ISM, filed the suit on October 16 in New York federal court. Sony is the sole defendant. Chris Brown is not being sued in this case.

The dispute centers on the 2016 song with Usher and Gucci Mane. The suit said his deal with Chris Brown Entertainment gave ISM a 1.5% royalty. That was his share after a split with fellow producer A1. Sony paid his share but used a rate of 0.75%, the filing claims.

The suit links that claim to a July review of his records. ISM flagged the gap to Sony in August. That review said he got about half the pay he was due for the last period.

The cash demand goes beyond that claimed shortfall. ISM said he sold royalty interests to Xposure Music Holdings in June. The deal called for Sony to send checks to the buyer from September 1 onward. His suit claims Sony stalled the payee change for six weeks and held up that sale.

“The compensation sought is not a computation of royalties; it is what the conduct cost, and what it would have cost Sony to obtain those concessions honestly,” the complaint stated.

Much of the fight turned on the terms of a form. The suit says Sony asked him to sign a form that said the payee had no right to audit Sony or its affiliates. Staff called the terms fixed rules. But, by his account, a form with those terms cut was already in Sony’s files.

The filing also points to a clash in what Sony told his team. On July 24, staff said there was no account for his share, according to the suit. Four days later, Sony confirmed it was accounting for the Chris Brown track. He cited years of Sony statements as proof that the account was there all along.

ISM claimed those weeks of talks put pressure on him to take Sony’s terms. He signed the new form on August 29 but said he did not give up his claims.

“On August 29, 2026, plaintiff executed the form Sony produced. The executed instrument contains no release, no waiver, and no acknowledgment of any account,” the complaint stated.

Sony’s in-house lawyer denied liability on October 15 and called the matter “fully resolved,” according to the complaint. The suit seeks at least $1,247,500 for the harm claimed, plus punitive damages on the fraud counts. ISM also asked the court to order an audit and award any unpaid funds it finds.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Gets New Shot At Fighting Nine-Month Prison Sentence
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa cleared a court hurdle in his fight against a nine-month Romanian prison sentence, with a new hearing set for October 29.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa won a new chance to fight his nine-month prison term in Romania. The guilty verdict still stands.

The Bucharest court let one part of his bid move forward Tuesday. It threw out a second part. The court will take up his bid next week.

The case stems from July 2024, when Wiz smoked weed on stage in Costinesti. Tuesday’s ruling let him claim that the court had failed to stick to the rules.

The court’s case record states, translated from Romanian: “Pursuant to Article 431 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, in conjunction with Article 426(a) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, [the court] admits, in principle, the annulment challenge filed by T.C.J. against criminal decision No. 1222/P of December 18, 2025, issued by the Constanta Court of Appeal in case No. 7777/118/2024.”

The court used T.C.J. for Wiz’s name.

The part of his bid that cleared this first stage deals with notice of a court date. The law covers those who were not told of the court date in the right way. Those who were told of the date can also bring this claim if they could neither be there nor tell the court why.

Judges have not ruled that this happened in Wiz’s case. They let that claim pass the first test so they can hear it on its merits.

The same order adds: “Pursuant to Article 432(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, [the court] sets a hearing for the annulment challenge on October 29, 2026, at 1 P.M., for which the defendant’s chosen lawyer shall be notified.”

Wiz first faced a fine of 3,600 lei. The state pushed for jail time. The Constanta Court of Appeal sentenced him to nine months in December 2025. He was found guilty of having weed for his own use.

He failed to get the jail term thrown out in February. The top court sent the case to Bucharest in September.

The court took up this first stage last week but did not rule on it until Tuesday. His next chance to ask for the sentence to be thrown out is October 29.

item.title: Macklemore Faces Backlash Over Palestine Tour Beneficiary’s October 7 Remarks
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Macklemore's Palestinian benefit tour drew demands for Live Nation to explain its vetting of a group over October 7 remarks.
item.content:encoded:
Macklemore‘s plans to raise funds for Palestine drew fire over how one group spoke of the October 7 attacks. Two Jewish groups asked Live Nation to explain how it checked who would get the money.

The rapper’s “Free Palestine Tour” is set to raise funds for 12 groups. One is the Palestinian Youth Movement, which called the Hamas-led attacks a “prison break.”

The Jewish Leadership Council asked what checks had been made. It also sought steps to make sure funds would not back threats to Jews.

“When the PYM describes the 7 October massacre as a ‘prison break’, it risks legitimizing violence against Jews,” the council told The Jewish Chronicle last week.

The Israeli-American Council also asked Live Nation to explain its checks and block funds to groups that justified violence, Fox News Digital reported.

The phrase came from an essay the youth group wrote for The New Inquiry. It ran on October 7, 2024, one year after the attacks. The piece framed the attack through Gaza’s blockade and the loss of homes and land. It cast the fighters as people going back to land their families once held. It did not address civilians killed or taken hostage in Israel.

On its own site, the group says it works for freedom and helps fund food and water for Gaza. It said a past drive with 10 partners raised $1 million in two months. That helped fund an average of 10,000 hot meals a day and more than 1 million gallons of water, it said. The group gave those figures in its own account of the past aid drive.

Macklemore, Live Nation and the group had not answered requests for comment when The Jerusalem Post carried the report.

The rapper had said his stance on Israel did not target Jews. He spoke while on tour with Ed Sheeran in September. He said his aim was peace and equal treatment for all. Those remarks came before the dispute over who would get the funds.

Venues objected to his stage remarks, and he was dropped from the rest of Sheeran’s U.S. dates. He shared plans for his own shows on September 24. All proceeds would go to groups that support Palestine and its movement.

The three-show run starts in Dublin on October 26, then heads to Paris and London.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Feds Say Fake Central Cee Account Drew In Crypto Scam Victim
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: A fake Central Cee account allegedly lured a crypto victim as federal prosecutors sought more than 50,000 USDT in a new case.
item.content:encoded:
Central Cee‘s name was used to lure a crypto scam victim, a Secret Service agent alleged in a new federal case.

The British rapper was not accused of running the scheme. The agent said an account posed as him to draw a person into a private chat group.

Prosecutors filed the case in Puerto Rico on October 19. They sought 50,221.254086 USDT, a crypto token known as Tether. They said the funds were tied to wire fraud and money laundering. The suit seeks to take the funds through civil forfeiture.

Secret Service Agent Nayit Limery Gonzalez laid out the claims in a nine-page filing. The filing called the person who lost the funds Victim A. The person found Snapchat accounts that claimed to be stars, the agent wrote. Those accounts linked to Signal groups with tips on crypto prices.

One account used the name “centralceenewss” and posed as Central Cee, the filing said. Victim A then spoke on Signal with a person the agent called Subject A.

“Victim A stated that Subject A advised them that he manages a group that studies the trends of the crypto market. Subject A stated he does not want any money up front, but that he would request 15% of Victim A’s monthly earnings as a commission for the tips on the crypto market. Victim A stated that Subject A had a British accent when talking to him.”

Subject A then sent links that were passed off as crypto news apps, the filing said. He urged Victim A to use them.

“These links that appeared to be for cryptocurrency news applications were sent to Victim A directly from Subject A. Victim A clicked on all these links and downloaded the apps from the links provided.”

Gonzalez said scammers can hide harmful code in what seem to be real apps. That was not a finding that these links held such code. Nor did the agent accuse the real app firms of taking part in the scheme.

Victim A said 32,451.558669 USDT left their Trust Wallet without consent on July 12, 2024. That was not the same as the full sum sought in the case. The agent traced funds through several wallets, where some were mixed with other money.

Gonzalez signed the filing on October 1. More than two years had passed since the reported loss.

The Federal Trade Commission has warned of fake crypto deals pitched by people who pose as stars on social media. It urges people not to click links in messages they did not expect.

People can claim rights to seized funds in this type of case. The Justice Department has said those claims must be resolved first. Only then can the funds be forfeited and returned to victims.

The docket listed a request for a warrant and seizure. Responses were due November 2.
